pr_title: HTTP/3: Use max field section size setting

issue_context.title: HTTP/3: Use SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE setting
issue_context.body: Kestrel is sending SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE to the client but it isn't using SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE sent by the client.
comments:
Thanks for contacting us.

review_comments: I think this can be configured on the server with [MaxRequestHeadersTotalSize](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.server.kestrel.core.kestrelserverlimits.maxrequestheaderstotalsize?view=aspnetcore-5.0).

I think this makes sense. I wonder if we couldn't do the same for HTTP/2 and deprecate Http2Limits.MaxRequestHeaderFieldSize. For HTTP/2, It's used by HPackDecoder, but I don't really see the harm in using MaxRequestHeadersTotalSize for the same purpose.
They actually have different purposes. total size = total header section size. This property is specific to an individual header. I rolled the changes I had related to this back.

Yeah. And that's why we probably won't change it. I just think it was too fine grained of a knob that never needed exposing in the first place. We don't enforce a per-field or per-header limit for HTTP/1.x either. I don't see the harm in making the MaxRequestHeadersTotalSize also the max field size. Our defaults are pretty low anyway.

https://quicwg.org/base-drafts/draft-ietf-quic-http.html#header-size-constraints
> A server that receives a larger header section than it is willing to handle can send an HTTP 431 (Request Header Fields Too Large) status code

(HTTP/2) https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17861

We would like to implement 431s eventually, they're easier to understand than InternalError. Do we get a specific enough error back from the decoder to do that?

At least file an HTTP/3 specific issue for this.
